reader.decision: Approve the price.changed subscriber in every shop-api pod, with price_cache TTL reduced from 3600 to 300 as a backstop. Reject the CDN TTL change. Before merging, confirm where start_invalidation() is called in the shop.app startup.
reader.decision_reason: The message shows the CDN never caches /api/*, so my CDN proposal can't help. The stale price comes from per-pod caches that never hear about changes, and the subscriber fixes that cause using the existing event. The 300s TTL limits the gap left by Redis pub/sub not replaying messages.

reconstruction.problem: After a price change in the admin, customers see the old price for up to an hour. The CDN is not the cause, because cdn/rules.yaml:10-11 sets /api/* to cache: false. The cause is price_cache in pricing/service.py:5, a per-pod TTLCache with a 3600s TTL. shop-api runs 6 replicas, each with its own cache. update_price in admin/prices.py:14 pops the SKU only on the pod that served the admin request. It then publishes price.changed, but only search/indexer.py subscribes.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Only 1 of 6 pods shows the new price. The other 5 keep serving the old price until their own entries expire, up to 3600s after each fill. In the example, KET-2210 shows 39.90 until about 10:57 and checkout shows it until about 10:58, so customers pay the old price and reloads flip between values.
reconstruction.fix: In pricing/service.py add on_price_changed(event), which runs price_cache.pop(event['sku'], None), and start_invalidation(), which calls subscribe('price.changed', on_price_changed). Call start_invalidation() once per pod at shop-api startup. admin/prices.py stays unchanged. Also cut the price_cache TTL from 3600 to 300 as a backstop. Alternatives are ttl=60 (one line, up to 60s stale, more DB reads) or a shared Redis price cache (exact, but a Redis read per price call and a larger change).
reconstruction.cost: One Redis connection per pod. Redis pub/sub does not replay, so a pod that is disconnected during a publish stays stale until its TTL expires (up to 5 minutes with the 300s backstop). The shorter TTL adds some database reads. The startup call site is in shop.app, which is not in the repo, so it is unverified.

follow_up_questions: Where in shop.app does startup code live, and can start_invalidation() be called once per pod there?
Does subscribe() reconnect automatically after a Redis disconnect, or does a dropped connection silently stop invalidation?
reader.closing_answer: I approve the price.changed subscriber with price_cache TTL reduced to 300 as a backstop, not the one-line ttl=60 change. I also ask for the start_invalidation() call to be placed and verified in the shop.app startup, since that file is not in this repo.
